channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: The Stock Market’s Boom Will Likely Bust
item.description: It’s easy to make the case that the US equity market is in bubble territory when the major metrics point in the same direction. There are several reasons why this bubble will likely burst before the end of 2027. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Why Data Center Pushback Is a Unique Form of NIMBYism
item.description: Unlike solar farms or housing projects, data centers face a unique challenge: people don't just oppose them in their own backyards—they question if we need them at all. On Odd Lots, Jasmine Sun tells Joe Weisenthal and Tracy Alloway why the AI industry and policymakers have failed to make a compelling case for the AI buildout, leading to widespread anxiety over resource usage. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Odd Lots: Why Many Communities Are Skeptical of the AI Boom
item.description: From electrical contractors to HVAC engineers, people far from Silicon Valley are quietly asking the same question: Is AI a bubble? Speaking with Joe Weisenthal and Tracy Alloway on Odd Lots, Jasmine Sun explains how local communities weigh the massive economic tradeoffs of multi-year data center projects when they aren't even sure if the technology—or its funding—is here to stay. Listen wherever you get your podcasts. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apollo Reports Data Breach From ‘Social Engineering Incident’
item.description: Apollo Global Management Inc. said hackers breached its systems in July and accessed personal information, following a spate of attempted or successful cyberattacks at major hedge funds in recent weeks.
item.dc:creator: Laura Benitez

item.title: Anthropic Investor Blasts Traditional Venture Capital
item.description: Early Anthropic investor Anjney Midha unloads on traditional venture capital, arguing firms failed investors by missing the AI revolution. He explains why he’s still buying Anthropic, predicts public markets will embrace frontier AI, and reveals why Stripe’s OpenRouter acquisition may really be a massive bet on securing the agentic internet. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Uber Faces €825 Million Dutch Fine Over Driver Suspensions
item.description: Uber Technologies Inc. has been fined €825 million ($963 million) by Dutch authorities for using automated systems to suspend driver accounts, in what is the second-largest penalty under the European Union’s General Data Protection Regulation.
item.dc:creator: Charlotte Hughes-Morgan

item.title: Broadcom Seeking More Than $60 Billion in Latest AI Debt Deal
item.description: Broadcom is in talks to raise more than $60 billion in debt for an AI chip financing deal that will benefit Anthropic PBC and other companies. Ed Ludlow reports on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: DeepSeek Unveils Test Model to Rival Anthropic’s Opus 4.8
item.description: DeepSeek unveiled an experimental AI model that can understand visual prompts, saying the tool nears the performance of an advanced model by US rival Anthropic PBC.
item.dc:creator: Newley Purnell and Luz Ding

item.title: UK Bets on a Boom in AI Chip Newcomers
item.description: The government is helping fund some promising startups to gain a domestic foothold in the industry
item.dc:creator: Mark Bergen

item.title: Salesforce, ServiceNow Fight AI Fears With Buybacks and Bluster
item.description: Software companies are facing a crisis of confidence on Wall Street and trying increasingly aggressive strategies to address it.
item.dc:creator: Brody Ford

item.title: Samsung Plans to Return Up to $79 Billion to Shareholders
item.description: Samsung Electronics Co. expects to return as much as 110 trillion won ($79 billion) to shareholders this year, handing investors a chunk of the windfall generated by the AI rush. Tom Mackenzie reports on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Europe hands out state subsidies to fund domestic AI companies
item.description: Governments, fearful of missing out on the spoils of the AI boom, are funding local frontier labs, software and chip companies
item.dc:creator: Shona Ghosh

item.title: Japan Earmarks Another $944 Million for Rapidus in AI Chip Race
item.description: Japan’s government is allocating an additional ¥150 billion ($944 million) for chip startup Rapidus Corp., ramping up spending in a long-shot bid to compete against the likes of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.
item.dc:creator: Takashi Mochizuki

item.title: Humanoid Robots Put China Ahead in Tech Race
item.description:
China’s humanoid robot makers now control 97% of global shipments, giving Beijing an early lead over US rivals. But can they become everyday tools?
At the World Robot Conference in Beijing, robots sort boxes, handle laundry and bag clothes, as Allen Wan finds out. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: What the AI Industry Got Wrong About Public Backlash
item.description:
Even those within the AI industry have been very anxious about the technology. Worries about its potential to create destabilizing job losses, or rogue AI that could lead to human extinction. But for all their anxiety, they missed the thing that's become the most publicly salient: how upset people would be about data centers. Data center construction has been happening for a long time, and it used to be relatively uncontroversial. In fact, cities and states would often design their tax code to incentivize data center construction. On this episode, we speak with independent writer and Substacker Jasmine Sun, who recently traveled to Wisconsin and Michigan to report about the communities and activists trying to stop development, what the pushback is really all about and what future developers will have to do in order to be welcomed in.
See Odd Lots Live in LA September 2026 https://events.bloombergevents.com/event/ODDLOTSLA/summary (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Alphabet Bond Buyer Warns on Australia’s Capacity for AI Debt
item.description: Australian state-owned investment manager QIC Ltd., which invested in Alphabet Inc.’s debut Aussie dollar bond, expects more Big Tech issuance Down Under but cautions the market probably has only room for “a couple” such mega deals a year.
item.dc:creator: Amy Bainbridge and Matthew Burgess

item.title: Nvidia in Talks With Chip Startup Rebellions for Potential Deal
item.description: Nvidia Corp. is in early discussions with the Korean AI chip designer Rebellions about possible collaborations, including a technical partnership, an investment or perhaps even an acquisition, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Yoolim Lee

item.title: Humanoid Robots Put China Ahead in Tech Race
item.description: China’s humanoid robot makers now control 97% of global shipments, giving Beijing an early lead over U.S. rivals. At the World Robot Conference, robots sort boxes, handle laundry, and bag clothes, but the real test is whether they can become everyday tools. Bloomberg’s Allen Wan has more. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Samsung Plans $80 Billion in Dividends, Buybacks After AI Gains
item.description: Samsung Electronics Co plans to return as much as 110 trillion won ($80 billion) to investors this year, joining SK Hynix Inc. in sharing an AI windfall and putting in motion the largest shareholder return program in South Korea’s history.
item.dc:creator: Yoolim Lee and Youkyung Lee

item.title: Nvidia to Pay AI Startup Poolside a $6 Billion License, Newcomer Says
item.description: Nvidia Corp. has agreed to pay $6 billion to license artificial intelligence models from Poolside and will extend job offers to more than 100 employees, according to people familiar with the situation.
item.dc:creator: Benoit Berthelot, Rebecca Torrence and Ian King
